title: Ionic vs Covalent — Electron Sharing vs Transfer
description: Compare sodium chloride (ionic lattice) with molecular covalent bonds like HCl and H₂.

steps.prompt: In sodium chloride (NaCl), how do sodium and chlorine achieve stable noble gas octets?
options: Sodium donates 1 electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions
They share an electron pair equally
steps.explanation: Correct! Sodium (2,8,1) readily loses its valence electron to chlorine (2,8,7). Electrostatic attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ forms an ionic bond.

steps.prompt: Inspect the NaCl ionic unit. Notice the large difference in size between the compact sodium cation and the large chloride anion.
steps.explanation: Losing an entire electron shell makes Na⁺ much smaller than the original Na atom, while adding an electron expands Cl⁻ due to electron-electron repulsion.

steps.prompt: Why do solid ionic compounds like NaCl have very high melting points compared to covalent molecules like methane?
options: Strong non-directional electrostatic forces extend throughout an entire 3D crystal lattice
Ionic compounds contain heavy metal nuclei
steps.explanation: In an ionic solid, every ion is surrounded by oppositely charged neighbors in a continuous crystal lattice, requiring immense thermal energy to break apart.
